normative_source: api/src/services/**/{sig,canonical-bytes,crypto,authority,elevate,tiers}.ts and api/src/routes/identity/at-rest.ts — the SERVER is the arbiter. Every canonical_hex below was produced by calling those functions.

conventions.canonical_hex: Lowercase hex of the EXACT bytes an ed25519 signature covers. For signed_bytes="sha256-digest" that is the 32-byte digest; for signed_bytes="utf8-message" it is the UTF-8 encoding of the canonical string.
conventions.rejects: The server itself refuses this input, so no canonical bytes exist. Every implementation must raise.
conventions.sdk_rejects: The server produces the pinned bytes, but both SDKs deliberately refuse the input. The SDK suites assert a raise; the server suite asserts the hex.
conventions.sdk_ts_skip: No TypeScript SDK function implements this format. The loader emits a named skip carrying this reason — never a silent omission.
conventions.binary_fields: Any field ending in _b64 is standard base64 of raw bytes; implementations decode before concatenating.

cases.name: ascii-baseline
cases.note: Two actions, deliberately unsorted on the way in.

cases.name: expires-at-null
cases.note: A perpetual grant. `expires_at ?? ""` means this MUST differ from the baseline and MUST collide with expires-at-empty-string.

cases.name: expires-at-empty-string
cases.note: Pins the null/empty collision rather than hiding it.

cases.name: scope-messy-normalizes-to-baseline
cases.note: Case, surrounding space, and duplicates are not grant meaning — this MUST reproduce ascii-baseline exactly.

cases.name: scope-count-binds-the-run-A
cases.note: Two actions, no expiry. Pairs with -B: without the count bound before the members, a variable-length field run could be re-split.

cases.name: scope-count-binds-the-run-B
cases.note: The re-split candidate. MUST NOT collide with -A.

cases.name: ids-non-ascii-bmp
cases.note: BMP text in both identifiers.

cases.name: ids-astral
cases.note: Astral-plane text — the surrogate-pair encoding probe.

cases.name: scope-sort-utf16-vs-codepoint
cases.note: The pair that separates a UTF-16 code-unit sort from a code-point sort. The scope is SORTED before framing, so a language sorting the other way produces a different digest here and nowhere else.

cases.name: scope-over-128-chars-truncated
cases.note: Normalization caps each action at 128 characters before framing.

cases.name: scope-truncation-counts-utf16-code-units
cases.note: The 128-character cap is 128 UTF-16 CODE UNITS, because the server truncates with JS `slice`. An astral character is one code point and two code units, so this 100-emoji action keeps 64 emoji, not 100. A language slicing by code point signs a longer action.

cases.name: scope-truncation-splits-a-surrogate-pair
cases.note: 127 units of filler plus an astral character puts the cap INSIDE a surrogate pair. JS `slice` leaves the lone leading surrogate and `TextEncoder` writes U+FFFD for it — so the signed bytes end in ef bf bd, and a language that raises here cannot sign this grant.

cases.name: scope-trim-is-the-javascript-whitespace-set
cases.note: The server trims in JavaScript. U+FEFF (ZWNBSP) IS trimmed there and is not by Python's str.strip(); U+0085 (NEL) and U+001C (FILE SEPARATOR) are NOT trimmed there and are by Python's. All three appear here, so a language using its own trim disagrees.

cases.name: scope-member-contains-nul-dropped
cases.note: A NUL-bearing action is DROPPED by normalization, not encoded — 0x00 is the field delimiter, so admitting it would let one scope member pose as the next. The count shrinks with it.

cases.name: nonce-contains-nul-delimiter
cases.rejects: canonicalDelegationBytesV2 throws: recipe-1 fields must not contain U+0000. The route refuses a NUL nonce before it gets here.

cases.name: scope-empty
cases.note: The server frames a zero-action grant as count "0".
cases.sdk_rejects: Both SDKs refuse an empty scope: an unbounded delegation is not expressible, so a caller grants '*' deliberately or grants nothing.

cases.name: delegator-id-empty
cases.note: The server frames an empty identifier.
cases.sdk_rejects: Both SDKs require delegator_id, delegate_id, and nonce to be non-empty — an anonymous side cannot be held to a grant.

formats.framing: sha256("memory-witness-issue/v1" || 0x00 || field ... in MEMORY_WITNESS_ISSUE_FIELD_ORDER; a null field is the literal text "null", numbers are base-10)

cases.name: ascii-baseline
cases.note: A 10000-unit USDC seal at the default 5% take-rate.

cases.name: memory-identity-null
cases.note: memory_identity_id is the one nullable field. A null is encoded as the literal text "null".

cases.name: memory-identity-literal-null-string
cases.note: The string "null" and a real null collide by construction: both render as "null". This vector pins that collision rather than pretending it is not there — it must equal memory-identity-null.

cases.name: non-ascii-bmp
cases.note: BMP text in the free-form DID, claim kind, and currency slots.

cases.name: astral
cases.note: Astral-plane text. The UTF-8 fold must be identical in both SDKs.

cases.name: currency-empty-string
cases.note: An empty field still occupies its slot: the NUL delimiters keep the field count fixed, so this is not the same digest as a missing field.

cases.name: amounts-all-zero
cases.note: A free seal. 0 + 0 = 0 satisfies the fee-split guard.

cases.name: rate-bps-at-ceiling
cases.note: 10000 bps is the whole thing. The guard is at-most, not less-than.

cases.name: claim-kind-contains-nul
cases.note: 0x00 is the field delimiter. A field carrying one could impersonate the next.
cases.rejects: memory-witness signed field must not contain NUL

cases.name: witness-did-contains-nul
cases.note: Same delimiter wall from the other side of the digest.
cases.rejects: memory-witness signed field must not contain NUL

cases.name: content-sha-uppercase
cases.note: The content hash is 64 LOWERCASE hex characters; uppercase is a different spelling of the same bytes and is refused rather than folded.
cases.rejects: memory_content_sha256 must be 64 lowercase hex characters

cases.name: tier-pair-not-authorized
cases.note: v1 authorizes foundational to constitutive and nothing else.
cases.rejects: memory-witness/v1 only authorizes foundational to constitutive

cases.name: fee-split-does-not-add-up
cases.note: platform_fee + net_amount must equal gross_amount, or the signature would authorize an arithmetic the parties never agreed.

cases.name: rate-bps-over-ceiling
cases.note: More than 100% is not a rate.

cases.name: gross-amount-negative
cases.note: Amounts are non-negative safe integers.
cases.rejects: gross_amount must be a non-negative safe integer

cases.name: expiry-missing-milliseconds
cases.note: Canonical is exactly what Date.prototype.toISOString emits — second-precision is not it.
cases.rejects: authorization_expires_at must be canonical ISO-8601 UTC

cases.name: expiry-impossible-calendar-date
cases.note: February 30th round-trips to March 2nd, so it is not canonical.
cases.rejects: authorization_expires_at must be canonical ISO-8601 UTC

formats.framing: sha256("attestation-issue/v1" || 0x00 || field ... in ATTESTATION_ISSUE_FIELD_ORDER; a null field is the literal text "null", numbers are base-10)

cases.name: ascii-baseline
cases.note: A 1500-unit GBP review at the default 5% take-rate, valid one year.

cases.name: validity-and-expiry-null
cases.note: The two nullable slots are null together: an attestation that never expires. Both render as the literal text "null".

cases.name: claim-is-the-text-null
cases.note: Rendering makes a real null and the four-character string "null" indistinguishable WITHIN a slot. Nothing collides here because claim is never nullable — this vector pins that the collision is per-slot, so nullability must be read from the field list, not from the bytes.

cases.name: non-ascii-bmp
cases.note: BMP text in the free-form DID, claim, and currency slots.

cases.name: astral
cases.note: Astral-plane text. The UTF-8 fold must be identical in both SDKs.

cases.name: claim-contains-linefeed
cases.note: 0x0A is not the delimiter and is not folded away: a multi-line claim signs as written.

cases.name: amounts-all-zero
cases.note: A free attestation. 0 + 0 = 0 satisfies the fee-split guard.

cases.name: take-rate-at-ceiling
cases.note: 10000 bps is the whole thing. The guard is at-most, not less-than.

cases.name: amounts-at-safe-integer-ceiling
cases.note: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER is the largest amount both runtimes spell the same way in base 10.

cases.name: validity-one-second
cases.note: The smallest legal validity. Positive, not merely non-negative.

cases.name: claim-contains-nul
cases.note: 0x00 is the field delimiter. A field carrying one could impersonate the next.

cases.name: attester-did-contains-nul
cases.note: Same delimiter wall from the other side of the digest.

cases.name: grant-currency-empty
cases.note: Unlike memory-witness-issue/v1, this format refuses an empty text slot outright: a settlement with no named currency is not a settlement.

cases.name: subject-did-empty
cases.note: An attestation about nobody is not an attestation.

cases.name: listing-id-uppercase-uuid
cases.note: UUID slots are lowercase hex. Uppercase is a different spelling of the same identifier and is refused rather than folded.

cases.name: evidence-sha-uppercase
cases.note: The evidence hash is 64 LOWERCASE hex characters.

cases.name: fee-split-does-not-add-up
cases.note: platform_fee + attester_net must equal grant_gross, or the signature would authorize an arithmetic the parties never agreed.

cases.name: take-rate-over-ceiling
cases.note: More than 100% is not a rate.

cases.name: grant-gross-negative
cases.note: Amounts are non-negative safe integers.

cases.name: validity-seconds-zero
cases.note: Zero seconds of validity is an already-expired claim, not a claim.

cases.name: validity-null-but-expiry-set
cases.note: The two nullable slots move together. A never-expiring attestation cannot carry an expiry.

cases.name: validity-set-but-expiry-null
cases.note: And the same disagreement from the other side.

cases.name: authorization-expiry-missing-milliseconds
cases.note: Canonical is exactly what Date.prototype.toISOString emits — second-precision is not it.

cases.name: attestation-expiry-impossible-calendar-date
cases.note: February 30th round-trips to March 2nd, so it is not canonical.
